result.title: Triage Accuracy of Jev and Open-Weight System One Decision Models and Their Use for Early Emergency Recognition in Symptom-Assessment Applications
result.summary: Laypeople increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for triage advice, but LLMs answer in variable free text, which makes it hard to evaluate them for use in medical devices. Decision models, which assign a probability to each predefined triage category, may be easier to evaluate. To test their triage accuracy, we evaluated 16 decision models (14 open-weight, 2 proprietary) on 233 synthetic and 10,000 real-world cases, yielding 163,728 total assessments. The best models triaged 72.1% of synthetic cases correctly and agreed with an existing algorithm in 56.1% of real-world cases. They were more promising for recognising emergencies early: given only demographics, chief complaints, risk factors and red-flag answers, the best model reached an AUROC of 0.87. At a 5% error margin, it could decide for or against emergencies for about half of users. Decision models should therefore not replace triage engines but could shorten symptom assessments at setting-specific error margins.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文评估 16 个决策模型（多数为开权重模型）在合成与真实分诊病例上的分类准确性与与既有算法的符合度，并考察仅凭有限信息（人口学、主诉、风险因素、红旗答案）早期识别急症的能力。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「在给定误差边界下对约半数用户即可作出判断、从而缩短问诊」的准确率—覆盖率权衡，可能为 LVR 中「何时停止获取证据再作答」的停止决策与选择性预测提供类比线索，但论文不涉及 latent 状态或视觉推理，需较多核查。
